summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted for a clogged gastrojejunal tube and low-grade fever. He had recently completed treatment for a multidrug-resistant respiratory and urinary tract infection. On admission, his white blood cell count was elevated but without localizing signs of infection. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth, and he remained afebrile after presentation. The GJ tube was successfully replaced by interventional radiology and is functioning well. His recurrent C. difficile was managed with continued oral vancomycin, and he was monitored for potential drug interaction between linezolid and citalopram, with instructions to restart the latter one week after discharge. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, normalizing labs, and a working feeding tube.
problems: Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
